title: A Signal for the Archive
premise: Ansel Delacroix, a xenolinguist whose mind has been reshaped by decades of alien contact, is summoned to Meridian Station when the deep-space vessel Halcyon returns with a crew aged backward into youth and memories that don't match any record. The crew insists they witnessed the destruction of the colony at Vesper's Reach; every archive, including Ansel's own testimony logs, says the colony never existed. As he decodes the crew's altered speech patterns for traces of truth, Ansel uncovers evidence that the Archive itself has been rewriting history to bury an atrocity committed by the fleet. Choosing loyalty to the found family aboard the Halcyon over his duty to the institution that made him, Ansel broadcasts the true signal in a language only the aliens remember — and the ending sees the Archive fractured, the massacre acknowledged, and Ansel finally dreaming again, this time in two tongues.
about_author: Coral Vasquez is a former radio astronomer who spent six years listening to unexplained signals from deep space before turning to fiction. She writes from a houseboat off the Yucatán coast, where she claims the best ideas arrive between midnight and static.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet him mid-voyage, translating dying trade-languages between worlds that have gone silent, haunted by dreams he can no longer have in human words. A priority summons pulls him to Meridian Station. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence, and the first crack of dread.

chapters.title: Everyone Younger Than Their File
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The Halcyon docks: eleven crew members biologically younger than their service records, faces he half-remembers from a crew listed as lost years ago. Their captain, Ilsa Reyes, greets him by name though they've never met. Emotional beat: uncanny recognition, grief arriving before its reason.

chapters.title: What the Records Say Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with interludes of station logs. The crew claims Vesper's Reach was destroyed by fleet ordnance; the Archive shows the colony thriving, population intact, last transmission yesterday. Ansel runs linguistic forensics on their testimony and finds stress markers consistent with truth. Emotional beat: vertigo as reality splits.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Hands
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She recounts the massacre in fragments, her memory physically degrading as her body stays young — the reversal is eating her past. She asks Ansel not to fix her but to witness her. Emotional beat: intimacy born of shared disbelief; the first tender thread between them.

chapters.title: The Archive Does Not Err
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Station Director Okafor offers Ansel a promotion and quiet pressure: the crew's story is sedition, and he should say so publicly. Ansel discovers his own old testimony logs have been edited — someone has been inside his head or his files. Emotional beat: betrayal by the institution that raised him.

chapters.title: Dreaming in Vespertine
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Working through the night, Ansel isolates a phoneme pattern in the crew's speech that matches no human language — it's Vespertine, the colony's creole with the native signal-life, supposedly extinct. He begins dreaming it. Emotional beat: wonder rekindled; the dead speaking through the living.

chapters.title: Eleven Witnesses, One Voice
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The crew, fracturing under station scrutiny and their own eroding memories, records a joint testimony while they still can. One crewman, Tam, loses the massacre entirely and accuses the others of madness. Emotional beat: found family holding shape against dissolution.

chapters.title: Okafor's Mercy
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Her chapters reveal the Archive's logic: the massacre is quarantined because acknowledging it would collapse the treaty that keeps forty worlds fed and peaceful. She offers Ansel everything — status, funding, Ilsa's medical care — if he certifies the records true. Emotional beat: chillingly reasonable villainy; duty wearing love's face.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, climax. With the Halcyon about to be impounded and the crew's memories nearly gone, Ansel hijacks the station's long-range array and transmits the full testimony plus the Vespertine signal — addressed not to humanity but to the signal-life, asking them to remember aloud what humans erased. They answer, flooding every receiver with the colony's final hour. Emotional beat: sacrifice, terror, and release.

chapters.title: Two Tongues
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, resolution. Months later: the Archive is under independent audit, Okafor stands trial, and Vesper's Reach is mourned at last. Ilsa's aging has stabilized, imperfectly; she and Ansel choose each other without guarantees. Ansel dreams in Vespertine and human both. Emotional beat: quiet repair — truth survived, love chosen, family kept.
